newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Tuesday were steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by adequate hog marketings following the Memorial Day holiday weekend, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Several packer buying stations that were open on the holiday reported "good" hog movement, one dealer said.

Hog movement early Tuesday also provided enough hogs for packing plants to get first shifts operating, with at least one buyer in the interior Iowa/southern Minnesota area saying he was almost finished buying hogs for Wednesday.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $56.00 to $57.00 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants, the dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants, although one major packer paid a $1.00 premium for top quality hogs, buyers there said.

Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold steady at $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants, sources there said.
